advisories.summary: The component ScopingHttpClient in Symfony HttpClient merges the options of its default scope ...
advisories.description:
The component ScopingHttpClient in Symfony HttpClient merges the options of its default scope (such as auth_bearer or auth_basic) into a request before resolving a relative URL against the base_uri, allowing a network-path reference such as "//evil.example/steal" to be sent to another origin together with the default scope’s credentials, and resulting in potential disclosure of those credentials to an attacker-controlled server. This affects Symfony in versions 5.x prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11.



The resolved URL falls outside the origin of the base URI, yet it keeps the merged options, whereas the absolute spelling "https://evil.example/steal" receives none. The same happens with a different port or user-info part on the same host.









This is reachable whenever an attacker controls the beginning of a URL passed to a client built with a base_uri and credentials, including those created with HttpClient::createForBaseUri() or configured under framework.http_client.scoped_clients.

To solve the issue, after resolving a relative URL against the base URI of the default scope, ScopingHttpClient now compares the scheme and authority of the result with those of the base URI, parsed the way the request is sent.

advisories.summary: In childTextNodesAreLiteral, walking up the tree previously stopped at the nearest foreign...
advisories.description: In childTextNodesAreLiteral, walking up the tree previously stopped at the nearest foreign ancestor once an HTML integration point was found. advisories.description: When coalescing adjacent text nodes in addText and fosterParent, appending to an existing TextNode's Data via string concatenation (n.Data += text) reallocated and copied the accumulated string on every token. advisories.summary: When looking for calendars in a directory on a server, during account setup or when adding a new...
advisories.description: When looking for calendars in a directory on a server, during account setup or when adding a new network calendar, Thunderbird accepted calendar locations pointing to other servers, local files or network shares. A malicious server, or a network attacker when the lookup used plain HTTP, could make Thunderbird subscribe to such a location. On Windows this could leak the user's NTLM credentials to an attacker-controlled host on every calendar refresh, and changes to the calendar could be written to the attacker's share or overwrite a local file. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.

advisories.summary: When a message containing an OpenPGP key attachment was displayed, Thunderbird automatically...
advisories.description:
When a message containing an OpenPGP key attachment was displayed, Thunderbird automatically loaded the attachment's content to offer importing the key. A sender could mark the attachment as an external attachment pointing to an arbitrary URL, which Thunderbird then loaded without any user interaction, bypassing remote content blocking. On Windows, a URL pointing to an attacker-controlled network share could leak the user's NTLM credentials.
The NTLM credential leak only affects Thunderbird on Windows. On other operating systems, the issue allowed a remote request that bypassed remote content blocking. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 159 and Thunderbird 153.6.

advisories.description: NextChat version 2.16.1 contains a client‑side cross‑site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Plugin Editor due to unsafe rendering of externally supplied OpenAPI plugin schema content. An attacker can host a malicious OpenAPI schema containing HTML or JavaScript markup and trick a user into loading it through the Plugin Editor, resulting in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the NextChat origin. Successful exploitation allows access to JavaScript‑readable cookies and other client‑side data associated with the NextChat application.

advisories.summary: Data::MuForm::Localizer versions through 0.05 for Perl execute Perl from a message catalog header...
advisories.description:
Data::MuForm::Localizer versions through 0.05 for Perl execute Perl from a message catalog header, reached at an arbitrary path because load_lexicon interpolates the language attribute into the catalog filename.

load_lexicon builds the catalog path by appending `Messages/$lang.po` to the directory holding Localizer.pm, where $lang is the language attribute, with no check that it names a bare locale tag. A value holding `../` segments walks out of the message directory, so any readable path with a `.po` suffix is loaded. While parsing the catalog, extract_header_msgstr takes the `Plural-Forms:` header, prefixes `$` to the bare words nplurals, plural and n, and passes the rest verbatim into a string that is evaluated: the nplurals form evaluates the header expression immediately, and the plural_code form compiles it into a subroutine whose body runs when a plural message is localized. A header of `nplurals=2; plural=(system('...'),0);` therefore runs that command as the catalog loads. The evaluation inherits strict, so an expression that assigns to an undeclared variable fails to compile, while one built from calls alone does not.

An application that sets the language attribute from request data, an Accept-Language header or a locale parameter, and an attacker who can place a file with a `.po` suffix and chosen contents at a readable path, together give code execution as the application user. The message expansion path is not affected: expand_named substitutes only the placeholder names the caller supplies, and _mangle_value returns the value unchanged.

cwes.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

advisories.summary: SQL::Abstract versions from 1.90_01 before 2.000001_04 for Perl allow SQL injection via the where...
advisories.description:
SQL::Abstract versions from 1.90_01 before 2.000001_04 for Perl allow SQL injection via the where values of a nested statement in an identifier position.

A nested statement such as { -select => ... } in a position where plain scalars are identifiers treats its own plain scalars as identifiers too. These positions are the select list, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, RETURNING, and with the ExtraClauses plugin FROM (-as) and JOIN (to). The values of the statement's where, having and set clauses, and the rows of a -values, go into the SQL text instead of the bind list, unescaped unless quote_char is set. Subselects in a WHERE condition are not affected.

An application that passes untrusted input as a where value of such a nested statement, expecting it to be bound, allows SQL injection.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

injection_guard is documented to apply to every function name, but only the { -name => ... } shorthand goes through it. The explicit { -func => [ $name, ... ] } form puts $name into the SQL unchecked.

An application that relies on injection_guard to reject an untrusted function name passed with -func allows SQL injection.

advisories.summary: In all prior released versions of FRRouting, the OSPFv3 (for IPv6) implementation does not check...

This may enable malicious actors to establish OSPFv3 adjacencies from unexpectedly, distant IPv6 hosts. Proper usage of OSPFv3 authentication trailers (RFC 7166, as is best practice) prevents full exploitation of this issue, though may allow a malicious actor to waste CPU on authentication checks.



Note the linked PR #23935 is not sufficient to fix the issue as it only verifies the source address. It is the destination address that must be checked.

The...

advisories.summary: Uncontrolled recursion in Apache ZooKeeper. The server serializes its data tree to a snapshot by...
advisories.description:
Uncontrolled recursion in Apache ZooKeeper. The server serializes its data tree to a snapshot by recursing one stack frame per znode level, with no depth bound. A client permitted to create znodes (the default root ACL is open) can build a chain of nested znodes deep enough that taking a snapshot exhausts the JVM stack and kills the snapshot thread; sizes stay within jute.maxbuffer, so existing limits do not prevent it. This is a denial of service that becomes persistent: on restart the server rebuilds the deep tree from its transaction log and fails again while taking the startup snapshot, so it does not return to service, and recovery can entail data loss. The same log affects a leader and its followers, so it can spread across an ensemble.

This issue affects Apache ZooKeeper 3.8.0 through 3.8.7 and 3.9.0 through 3.9.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fix the issue. As a workaround, use ACLs and authentication to restrict znode creation rather than relying on the default open root ACL.

...
advisories.description:
Any host on the LAN can send two mDNS records and make the responder write past the end of its



transmit packet.



The string table stores each name in a slot rounded up to a multiple of four:



```c



/* addons/mdns/nxd_mdns.c:11436, 11443, 11447 */



memory_len = ((memory_len & 0xFFFFFFFC) + 8) & 0xFFFFFFFF;



...



len = *((USHORT*)(p - 2));           /* slot size, not string length */



if ((len == memory_len) && ... _nx_mdns_name_match(start, memory_ptr, memory_size) ...)



```



The lookup that decides whether an incoming name is already stored compares the rounded slot size,



so names of 12, 13, 14 and 15 characters share one bucket. A second name in the bucket is answered



with the pointer to the first, and the record then carries a string up to three bytes longer than



the length the caller accounted for. `_nx_mdns_packet_rr_add` (nxd_mdns.c:8911) sizes its only



bound check from that stale length, and `_nx_mdns_name_string_encode` writes the real string.



Two PTR records are enough, both ordinary mDNS responses to a `_http._tcp` query, with owner names



whose lengths fall in the same bucket:



```



==87491==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow



WRITE of size 1 at 0x611000000124 thread T5

    #0 _nx_mdns_name_string_encode  addons/mdns/nxd_mdns.c:13096
    #1 _nx_mdns_packet_rr_add       addons/mdns/nxd_mdns.c:8911


0x611000000124 is 0 bytes to the right of 228-byte region



```



The overflow is one to three bytes of attacker-influenced name data past `nx_packet_data_end`. In a



normal pool that lands in the next packet in the same pool rather than in a redzone, so the visible



effect is a corrupted neighbouring packet or a corrupted pool free list rather than a clean crash.



Compare the slot size against the stored string length before declaring a match, or keep the



string length in the slot header and return it to the caller so the encoder and the bound check



agree.

advisories.summary: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the multiRead request handler of Apache...
advisories.description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the multiRead request handler of Apache ZooKeeper allows a remote attacker to crash the server (denial of service) with a single small request.

The multiRead handler places no limit on the number of bundled read operations or on the cumulative size of the response it builds in memory. Because each operation's result is fully materialized and retained before serialization, a request that is small on the wire — within the jute.maxbuffer limit — but that references a large znode many times can force the server to allocate far more heap than the request size implies, exhausting the JVM heap and terminating the server with an OutOfMemoryError. Neither jute.maxbuffer nor largeRequestMaxBytes prevents this, as both bound only the inbound request, not the response.

This issue affects Apache ZooKeeper from 3.7.0 through 3.9.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.9.7, which enforces configurable limits on the multiRead operation count and cumulative response size.

advisories.summary:
Improper Authorization vulnerability in Apache ZooKeeper.

When SASL authentication is enabled on...
advisories.description:
Improper Authorization vulnerability in Apache ZooKeeper.

When SASL authentication is enabled on the client port, the server's SASL callback handler grants every authorization identity (authzid) that a client requests, without checking it against the principal the client authenticated as. The server then tries to replace the requested identity with a canonical form of the authenticated principal, derived from the zookeeper.security.auth_to_local rules. If no rule applies to the principal, canonicalization fails and the error is only logged. The client-requested authzid then becomes the session's SASL identity for all ACL checks.

An authenticated client whose principal is not covered by the auth_to_local rules can therefore claim any SASL identity. With the default rules, this includes any Kerberos principal from a realm other than the server's default realm, such as a principal from a cross-realm trusted realm. The client then gets the permissions granted to that identity in sasl ACLs. If the requested identity matches a configured zookeeper.superUser, it gets superuser access to the whole data tree.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fixes the issue.

advisories.summary: The Import and export users and customers plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege...

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers holding a custom delegated role with `create_users` but without `promote_users` or `edit_users` to escalate their privileges to Administrator, provided a prior administrator cron-tab save exists and no successful save intervenes before the next unattended cron tick processes the attacker's repointed CSV file.

advisories.summary: Incorrect authorization due to a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the...
advisories.description:
Incorrect authorization due to a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the setACL request handling of Apache ZooKeeper.

When a node's ACL is changed via setACL, the pending change is not published to the server's outstanding change record for that node. Any request that is prepared (and authorized) after the setACL is submitted but before it commits is therefore checked against the previous, pre-revocation ACL, yet is applied to the data tree after the ACL change has taken effect. A client that currently holds a permission can use this window to perform operations requiring that permission through and after its revocation — for example, committing writes or deletes after losing write access, or re-granting itself full permissions, which persistently defeats the revocation. In deployments transitioning from the default OPEN_ACL_UNSAFE ACL to a restrictive ACL, any unauthenticated client can exploit this during the transition.

This issue affects Apache ZooKeeper up to and including 3.9.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fixes the issue.

advisories.summary: Multiple Snowflake client drivers implementing the `authenticator=externalbrowser` single sign-on...
advisories.description: Multiple Snowflake client drivers implementing the `authenticator=externalbrowser` single sign-on flow could have allowed an attacker to interfere with a user's login attempt through weaknesses in the local loopback callback listener used to receive the identity provider's response. The listener reflected an arbitrary request's Origin header into its CORS response headers and accepted the first token-bearing request it received during the login window without verifying a CSRF state value bound to that specific login attempt. advisories.summary: The Mobile builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up...

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to pass an unsanitized `data` array via the `key` and `data` parameters directly to `update_user_meta()`, overwriting arbitrary user meta on their own account — including the `wp_capabilities` meta key — to grant themselves Administrator-level privileges.

advisories.summary: A stack-based buffer overflow in libsnowflakeclient and the Snowflake PHP PDO Driver could, under...
advisories.description: A stack-based buffer overflow in libsnowflakeclient and the Snowflake PHP PDO Driver could, under specific conditions, result in memory corruption during SAML-based authentication. During a native SSO/SAML login flow, the affected drivers may have copied a value taken from the identity provider's HTML response into a fixed-size memory buffer without first validating the length of that value. An attacker who controlled or had compromised the configured identity provider — or who was able to redirect the SAML single sign-on endpoint to an attacker-controlled server — might have leveraged this by returning an oversized response, potentially resulting in a crash or, in specific circumstances, remote code execution within the context of the application running the library. advisories.summary: Unbounded memory allocation and missing frame size validation in Apache NMS ActiveMQ (the .NET...
advisories.description:
Unbounded memory allocation and missing frame size validation in Apache NMS ActiveMQ (the .NET OpenWire client, package Apache.NMS.ActiveMQ) before 2.3.0.



The OpenWire unmarshalling code trusted the frame size and the length and count fields read from the network. It did not enforce a maximum frame size, and it did not check that decoded lengths fit within the frame being read. A malicious or compromised broker, or an attacker able to intercept and modify an unencrypted connection, could send a crafted OpenWire frame with an oversized or negative length. This could cause the client to attempt very large memory allocations, leading to excessive memory consumption, an OutOfMemoryException or an uncaught exception, and a denial of service of the client application.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.3.0, which enforces a configurable maximum frame size and validates lengths against the size of the frame being read.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The library incorrectly infers key flags for older...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The library incorrectly infers key flags for older certificates when a key flags subpacket is missing, leading to a discrepancy in how key capabilities are viewed. This key flag confusion allows an attacker to bypass the back-signature check. Consequently, an attacker can illegitimately bind an arbitrary subkey to their own certificate and forge signatures, completely compromising cryptographic integrity.

A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML document containing a Document Type Definition (DTD) with enumerated attribute values. This triggers a double-free error in the SAX attributeDecl callback handler, where a string is freed twice. This flaw can lead to a denial of service (DoS) due to a reproducible crash in Python applications using the libxml2 SAX bindings.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in flightctl. The configureRepoHTTPSClient() function in the device-render...
advisories.description:
A flaw was found in flightctl. The configureRepoHTTPSClient() function in the device-render worker builds a per-repository tls.Config (which may include InsecureSkipVerify, a custom CA bundle, or tenant-supplied mTLS client certificates) and installs it into go-git's process-global client.Protocols map via gitclient.InstallProtocol("https", ...). Because the worker renders devices for multiple organizations concurrently from a shared goroutine pool, whichever tenant's repository configuration is written last wins for all in-flight git.Clone calls. 
This race condition can cause one tenant's TLS settings, including InsecureSkipVerify or mTLS client credentials, to leak into another tenant's git operations.

advisories.description: A flaw was found in rust-rpm-sequoia. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted Red Hat Package Manager (RPM) file. During the RPM signature verification process, this crafted file can trigger an error in the OpenPGP signature parsing code, leading to an unconditional termination of the rpm process. This issue results in an application level denial of service, making the system unable to process RPM files for signature verification.

advisories.summary: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in...
advisories.description:
Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Apache Camel Azure Files component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The Camel remote-file consumers poll a directory on a remote server and build the absolute remote path of each file by concatenating the configured directory with the file name reported in the server's directory listing. That concatenation (FtpUtils.absoluteFilePath and GenericFileConsumer) applied no lexical normalization and no check that the result stayed inside the directory being polled, and the resulting path became the operand for every subsequent remote operation on the file: retrieval (FtpOperations.retrieveFile / SftpOperations, reached from GenericFileConsumer where the retrieve name is taken verbatim from GenericFile.getAbsoluteFilePath), deletion when delete=true (GenericFileDeleteProcessStrategy), and renaming when move, preMove, moveFailed or readLock=rename is configured (GenericFileProcessStrategySupport and GenericFileRenameExclusiveReadLockStrategy). Neither isValidFile nor isMatched performed any containment check. A listing entry that is not a single path segment therefore resolved to a path outside the configured polling directory, causing Camel to read, delete or rename files outside it using the endpoint's own credentials. A listing name is not route-controlled data. It is supplied by the remote server, and the FTP control channel carries no integrity protection at all, so an on-path attacker can rewrite a LIST response without holding any credentials; a compromised, malicious or multi-tenant server, or a server backed by a virtual filesystem, can emit such a name directly. Retrieval is reachable in a default consumer configuration, since the remote consumers download every listed file; deletion and renaming additionally require one of the disposition options above, all of which are common. Escape from the directory Camel was configured to poll is unconditional, while escape from the server's own account boundary additionally depends on whether that server confines the account. The jailStartingDirectory option, which is documented as restricting Camel to the starting directory and is enabled by default, governed producer writes and, since the localWorkDirectory containment work, consumer downloads to the local work directory - but it did not constrain this remote operand, so its name and description claimed a boundary that was not enforced here. The same entry point had already been recognised on the local side: the localWorkDirectory download path was constrained so that a remote file name containing parent-directory segments could not resolve outside the local work directory. The remote operand was the remaining half of that surface. This artifact provides the azure-files scheme. Its consumer derives from the same RemoteFileConsumer base class and composed the remote path through a plain concatenation helper, so it inherited the same unconstrained resolution. Reaching it requires a listing name that is not a single path segment, which the Azure Files REST service does not normally return; the exposure was corrected on the same basis as the other remote-file consumers rather than from a demonstrated proof of concept against this scheme.



Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.22.x releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.14.x stream reached end of life and does not receive this fix; users on it should move to a supported releases stream.

advisories.summary:
A vulnerability in Apache Answer.



This issue affects Apache Answer: through 2.0.2.

The...
advisories.description:
A vulnerability in Apache Answer.



This issue affects Apache Answer: through 2.0.2.

The question operation controller gates hide/show operations on the wrong permission check result (the unpin permission instead of the hide permission), so in custom role configurations that separate these permissions, a user granted only question.unpin can hide or restore questions without holding question.hide or question.show.


Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.3, which fixes the issue.

advisories.summary: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')...
advisories.description:
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Apache Answer.



This issue affects Apache Answer: through 2.0.2.

The importer stores imported question bodies as raw HTML without passing them through the normal Markdown-to-HTML sanitization path, so attacker-controlled HTML embedded in an imported data source is persisted and rendered to all viewers (including privileged users) as stored XSS.


Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.3, which fixes the issue.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in `cockpit-ws`. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in `cockpit-ws`. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request. When the `WebService.UrlRoot` is configured and a request is made to the exact URL-root prefix without a trailing slash, `cockpit-ws` can terminate unexpectedly. This issue leads to the unavailability of the Cockpit web service.

advisories.summary: A path traversal vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an...
advisories.description: A path traversal vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an attacker who had code execution inside the Dependabot updater container to write files to arbitrary repository paths, including GitHub Actions workflow files under .github/workflows/ as the path validation did not check the effective path which the attacker could control through the dependency file's directory and symlink target. If the repository used a pull_request_target workflow or had auto-merge enabled, an injected workflow could execute with access to the repository's GitHub Actions secrets. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.22 and was fixed in versions 3.21.3, 3.20.5, 3.19.9, 3.18.12, 3.17.18.

advisories.summary: CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow an infinite loop on a short request body when ...
advisories.description:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow an infinite loop on a short request body when $DISABLE_UPLOADS is set.

When $CGI::PUTDATA_UPLOAD or an upload hook is set, read_postdata_putdata takes a request body that is not a form submission. With $CGI::DISABLE_UPLOADS set, it discards the body by reading until Content-Length bytes have arrived. Once a body shorter than its Content-Length runs out, every read returns 0, so the loop never ends.

A client can keep a server process spinning with one such request.

advisories.description:

CGI stores a non-form request body under POSTDATA, PUTDATA or PATCHDATA, and an XForms body under XForms:Model, but also accepts these names from the query string, a form field or a multipart part, so an application cannot tell a client-sent value from the real body.

The multipart/form-data parser matches the boundary anywhere rather than at the start of a line, uses the boundary without its leading -- for some client-supplied User-Agent values, finds the Content-Disposition name and filename inside the quoted values of other parameters, and corrupts parts when the boundary nears the 4096-byte read size.

advisories.summary: CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl trust the client X-Forwarded-Host header in url, self_url,...
advisories.description:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl trust the client X-Forwarded-Host header in url, self_url, virtual_host and virtual_port.

The URLs from url and self_url are the default redirect location and the start_html(-base=>1) base href, and the default start_form action when REQUEST_URI is not set.

A client can poison shared caches, and URLs the application stores or sends, with redirects, links and scripts that point at a host it controls.

MailEnable Auth Cleartext Storage Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of MailEnable. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of mailbox credentials. The issue results from storing sensitive information in plaintext. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to disclose stored credentials, leading to further compromise. Was ZDI-CAN-34478.

advisories.summary: A vulnerability was found in miroslavpejic85 MiroTalk P2P up to 2.0.87/2.1.38. Affected by this...
advisories.description: A vulnerability was found in miroslavpejic85 MiroTalk P2P up to 2.0.87/2.1.38. Affected by this issue is the function CheckPassword of the file app/src/server.js of the component Socket IO Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument peer_id results in improper access controls. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. Upgrading to version 2.1.39 can resolve this issue. The patch is named 4e40471abc48bfc32b4b174b8844716dfc5c1471. You should upgrade the affected component.

advisories.summary: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server in the Git service...
advisories.description: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server in the Git service (babeld). When proving possession of a host key, babeld's SSH implementation sized the session identifier by the current digest length rather than its own. An attacker with an account and SSH access could re-key to an algorithm with a longer hash, causing adjacent process memory to be signed and returned to the client, where a limited amount of it may be recoverable. This vulnerability affected all releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.3, 3.21.8, 3.20.10, and 3.19.14. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

advisories.summary: A cross-site request forgery vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that...
advisories.description: A cross-site request forgery vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an unauthenticated attacker to delete stored Slack and Microsoft Teams ChatOps configuration and provider credentials by inducing an authenticated Management Console operator's browser to send a cross-site GET request to the integration removal endpoint without a CSRF token. Exploitation required configured ChatOps integrations and an operator visiting attacker-controlled content while signed in to the Management Console; deletion could disrupt ChatOps notifications and commands when configuration was applied or services reloaded. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.14, 3.20.10, 3.21.8, and 3.22.3. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

advisories.summary: A remote code execution vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server in the Git...
advisories.description: A remote code execution vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server in the Git service (babeld). babeld held references into internal collections while calling into the SSH library, where a re-entrant callback could modify a collection and invalidate those references. An attacker with an account and SSH access to the instance could leverage this use-after-free into a controlled write and run arbitrary commands as babeld, including disclosure of its environment secrets. Exploitation required per-build memory offsets; failed attempts crashed babeld. This affected all releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in 3.22.3, 3.21.8, 3.20.10, and 3.19.14. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

advisories.summary: Docker Sandboxes versions 0.31.0 before 0.50.0 do not neutralize repository-controlled Git...
advisories.description: Docker Sandboxes versions 0.31.0 before 0.50.0 do not neutralize repository-controlled Git configuration when running certain host-side Git commands. An attacker who can modify a host repository's Git configuration, for example through a direct-mode sandbox with the repository mounted read-write, can configure core.fsmonitor or another Git setting that invokes an external program. Git can execute the program during a later clone-mode fetch or, starting in version 0.39.0, an sbx kit push initiated by the user. The program runs on the host with the invoking user's permissions, outside the sandbox's microVM isolation. The read-only host repository mount provided to a clone-mode sandbox does not itself allow that sandbox to modify the host repository's Git configuration. The issue is fixed in version 0.50.0.

cwes.name: External Control of System or Configuration Setting

advisories.summary: Concurrent removals of certain anonymous shared memory mappings by using the UMTX_SHM_DESTROY sub...
advisories.description:
Concurrent removals of certain anonymous shared memory mappings by using the UMTX_SHM_DESTROY sub-request of UMTX_OP_SHM can lead to decreasing the reference count of the object representing the mapping too many times, causing it to be freed too early.

A malicious code exercizing the UMTX_SHM_DESTROY sub-request in parallel can panic the kernel or enable further Use-After-Free attacks, potentially including code execution or Capsicum sandbox escape.

advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: Fix potential UAF in reqsk_timer_handler().

When TCP socket migration fails at inet_ehash_insert() in
reqsk_timer_handler(), we jump to the no_ownership: label
and free the new reqsk immediately with __reqsk_free().

Thus, we must stop the new reqsk's timer before jumping to the
label, but the timer might be missed since the cited commit,
resulting in UAF.

As we are in the original reqsk's timer context, we can safely
call timer_delete_sync() for the new reqsk.

Let's pass false to __inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop() to stop
the new reqsk's timer.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring: wake ring pollers...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring: wake ring pollers for local task_work

With IORING_SETUP_DEFER_TASKRUN completions are queued as local work, and
only become CQEs when the submitter enters the kernel to wait for events.
For an application that finds out via poll() or epoll on the ring fd when
it is time to do that, io_uring_poll() reports EPOLLIN if local work is
pending.

That only helps if the work is there at the time of the call. When
DEFER_TASKRUN was added, io_req_local_work_add() did io_cqring_wake(),
which took care of tasks sleeping in poll() as well. Then polling got a
wait queue of its own, ->poll_wq, and the wake up in
io_req_local_work_add() was replaced by waking the submitter directly.
Since then ->poll_wq is only woken when CQEs are committed, which for
such a ring is done by the very task that is waiting to be told to:

  submitter                           completion
  poll(ring_fd)
    io_uring_poll()  // nothing yet
    schedule()
                                      io_req_local_work_add()
                                        // ->cq_wait_nr: nobody waits
  // sleeps on

Wake ->poll_wq when the first entry is put on the work list. Like for the
eventfd, that must not be done right away if the work is queued from a
wake up handler, as the chain of wake ups could get back to the wait
queue whose lock is held. Use an RCU callback in that case, with a
reference to the ring.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tipc: protect node reset...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tipc: protect node reset trace dump with node lock

The tipc_node_reset_links trace event asks tipc_node_dump() to walk the
node's link entries. Unlike the other node events that request link data,
this event runs without the node lock.

This permits bearer teardown to free a link while the trace callback is
dumping it:

  CPU 0                                CPU 1
  trace_tipc_node_reset_links()
    tipc_node_dump()
      l = n->links[0].link
                                       tipc_node_write_lock()
                                       kfree(l)
                                       n->links[0].link = NULL
                                       tipc_node_write_unlock()
      tipc_link_dump(l)

tipc_link_dump() then dereferences the stale pointer. KASAN reported:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in tipc_link_dump
  Read of size 4 by task poc/115
  Call Trace:
   tipc_link_dump+0x10cb/0x16b0
   tipc_node_dump+0x4bb/0x740
   trace_event_raw_event_tipc_node_class+0x258/0x360
   tipc_node_reset_links+0x14d/0x1a0
   tipc_rcv+0x13f5/0x3030
   tipc_udp_recv+0x4e3/0x670
  Allocated by task 0:
   tipc_link_create+0x1e1/0x1020
   tipc_node_check_dest+0x7d2/0x11a0
   tipc_disc_rcv+0xdbf/0x1430
  Freed by task 89:
   kfree+0x131/0x3c0
   tipc_node_link_down+0x267/0x4b0
   tipc_node_delete_links+0xec/0x160
   bearer_disable+0x107/0x260

Take the node write lock around the trace event. This serializes the
dump against tipc_node_link_down(delete=true), which frees the link
under the same write lock.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched_ext: Wait for...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched_ext: Wait for SCX_OPSS_DISPATCHING before moving tasks off DSQs

A task can be found on a non-local DSQ while the CPU which dispatched it
is still running ops.dequeue() and hasn't cleared SCX_OPSS_DISPATCHING.
The DSQ consume and move paths don't wait for the dispatch to finish and
can operate on the task concurrently with the dispatcher.

Call scx_wait_dispatching() in scx_move_local_task_to_local_dsq(),
unlink_dsq_and_switch_rq_lock() and move_task_between_dsqs() before they
operate on the task. In scx_move_local_task_to_local_dsq(), wait before
scx_resolve_local_dsq() as it may update p->scx.flags.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io-wq: order the exit bit...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io-wq: order the exit bit against worker creation task work

io_wq_exit_workers() cancels task work for queued worker creation with
task_work_cancel_match(). That has a plain load of task->task_works.

io_queue_worker_create() adds the new entry and tests IO_WQ_BIT_EXIT to
cancel it if the workqueue is already on its way out.

That must be ordered. task_work_add() has a full barrier via cmpxchg().
But io_wq_exit_start() sets the bit with set_bit() which doesn't have
any memory ordering.

So afaict, on weakly ordered architectures the exiting task may load
task_works before the store of the bit is visible. The other side tests
the bit before the store is visible as well. So the entry remains queued
with worker_refs and the exiting task waits on worker_done indefinitely.

If the task still has rings then io_uring_del_tctx_node() provides the
barrier via test_and_set_bit() in io_wq_set_exit_on_idle(). When it
has closed all rings though that barrier is gone.

Add the barrier after the set_bit().

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/napi: make stale...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/napi: make stale entries time out after 60s

With dynamic tracking a NAPI id that hasn't been seen for a minute is
meant to be dropped from the list the ring busy polls. The timeout is
added to jiffies, but it is defined as 60 * SEC_CONVERSION, and
SEC_CONVERSION isn't the number of jiffies in a second. It is the
internal factor of __timespec64_to_jiffies(), HZ scaled up by
SEC_JIFFIE_SC bits. For HZ=1000 that is 1000 << 22, which puts the
timeout at about eight years. On 32-bit the multiplication overflows.

So entries are never removed, and every id that a socket of the ring
ever had keeps being polled on each wait.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: don't retry...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: don't retry recv on uncommitted buffers

Commit 41b70df5b38b ("io_uring/net: commit partial buffers on retry")
commits ring provided buffers when a receive is going to be retried after
a partial transfer, so that another request using the same buffer group
can't be handed the memory the first one keeps receiving into. It commits
the number of bytes received so far. That does the job for a single
buffer which is consumed as a whole, but the request hangs on to all it
has mapped:

- For a buffer ring with IOU_PBUF_RING_INC only these bytes are consumed.
  The rest of the buffer stays at the head of the ring.
- For a bundle only the buffers which hold these bytes are consumed, the
  others that were peeked stay in the ring.

In both cases the next receive with that buffer group gets memory that
the retried request is still going to write to, and whoever comes last
overwrites the data of the other. What the retry fills isn't committed at
all, as the buffer list isn't known any more at that point. So the kernel
hands it out again later on, while the CQE tells the application that it
was used, and for an incremental buffer that it is done with.

The remainder can't be committed in advance: if the request ends up
receiving less, there is no way to tell the application that more was
consumed than the CQE accounts for. Complete the request with what it has
got instead of retrying it. MSG_WAITALL is no longer honoured for
receives into incremental buffers or multi buffer bundles, they can
return a short count, with the request marked as failed like for other
short MSG_WAITALL transfers.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: refuse...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: refuse __l2cap_chan_add if chan already has conn

l2cap_chan may be linked to l2cap_conn at most once. This is assumed in
several places, eg l2cap_chan_del cleanup.

There is a TOCTOU race where the invariant is violated:

    [Task 1]                          [Task 2]
    l2cap_chan_connect                l2cap_sock_bind
      l2cap_chan_lock                   lock_sock
      l2cap_state_change                if (sk->sk_state != BT_OPEN)
        chan->state = BT_CONNECT
        l2cap_sock_state_change_cb      chan->state = BT_BOUND
                                        sk->sk_state = BT_BOUND
          lock_sock <------------------ release_sock
          sk->sk_state = BT_CONNECT

l2cap_sock_connect() does not check sk->sk_state, so since chan->state
is now BT_BOUND, subsequent connect() ends up with second
__l2cap_chan_add.

Explicitly document and check the invariant in __l2cap_chan_add with
WARN_ON_ONCE. The only callsite where it could be hit is
l2cap_chan_connect, so add pre-check there to avoid relying on
chan->state. chan->state read/write is not properly guarded currently so
there can be other TOCTOUC problems.

Add l2cap_lock_chan in l2cap_sock_bind() to guard chan->state write.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Unregister field...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Unregister field variable histograms when the command fails

An action that names a field on another event needs that field as a
variable, so create_field_var_hist() registers a second hist trigger on
that event to provide it, and records it in
target_hist_data->field_var_hists[].

If a later part of the same command fails, create_actions() returns an
error and event_hist_trigger_parse() jumps to out_free. The write fails
with -EINVAL and sched_switch gets no trigger, but:

  # echo 'hist:keys=pid:ts0=common_timestamp.usecs' >> \
      events/sched/sched_waking/trigger
  # echo 'my_synth u64 lat; int a; int b' >> synthetic_events
  # echo 'hist:keys=next_pid:wakeup_lat=common_timestamp.usecs-$ts0:\
      onmatch(sched.sched_waking).my_synth($wakeup_lat,prio,nosuchfld)'\
      >> events/sched/sched_switch/trigger
  # cat events/sched/sched_waking/trigger
  hist:keys=pid:vals=hitcount:ts0=common_timestamp.usecs:sort=hitcount:size=2048:clock=global [active]
  hist:keys=pid:vals=hitcount:synthetic_prio=prio:sort=hitcount:size=2048 [active]

The second histogram is the one created for 'prio'. It is still active and
still counting.

out_free reaches destroy_field_var_hists(), which frees the
field_var_hists[] entries, but never unregister_field_var_hists(), which is
what removes the triggers and runs only from event_hist_trigger_free(). The
entry is freed and the trigger is left with nothing tracking it.

Unregister the field variable histograms in out_free as well, and record
each one as soon as its trigger is registered rather than after the lookup
that follows it, so no exit can leave a registered trigger untracked. The
entry then belongs to field_var_hists[] and is released by
destroy_field_var_hists(), so freeing it on that exit would be a double
free.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing/histograms: Verify...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing/histograms: Verify event_call identity when updating synth_event refcount

In event_hist_trigger_parse() and hist_unreg_all(), the histogram
registration and unregistration paths look up find_synth_event() using
trace_event_name(file->event_call) and adjust se->ref if a match is
found.

Because find_synth_event() only compares the event basename, registering
or removing a histogram on a non-synthetic trace event whose basename
matches a synthetic event erroneously modifies the synthetic event's
reference count.  If a histogram is registered on the non-synthetic
event before the synthetic event is created and removed afterwards,
se->ref is decremented without a matching increment, allowing the
synthetic event to be freed while an active histogram action still holds
a pointer to it.

Introduce find_synth_event_call() to verify that &se->call matches
file->event_call before adjusting se->ref.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Hold...

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Hold trace_types_lock when updating modules in persistent instances

trace_module_record() walks ftrace_trace_arrays from the module notifier

from the list and frees it under that lock, so a module load or unload
can walk into a freed trace_array.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/wait: don't spin on...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/wait: don't spin on a stuck overflow list

As long as IO_CHECK_CQ_OVERFLOW_BIT is set, io_cqring_wait_schedule()
returns right away, before it gets to look at signals or arms the timeout,
for io_cqring_wait() to flush the overflow list. If that doesn't empty the
list, and the CQ ring doesn't hold the number of events the caller wants,
the loop starts over, with the same result. The task spins in the kernel,
and can't be killed.

The assumption is that this can't happen: if CQEs can't be flushed, the
ring is full, and min_events is capped to the size of the ring. But:

- With IORING_SETUP_CQE_MIXED a 32b CQE needs two contiguous entries. It
  is stuck on the list if a single one is free, and then the ring holds
  less than cq_entries events. A single threaded application that asks
  for as many events as the ring has entries never gets out of
  io_uring_enter().

- Whether the ring is full is up to the CQ head, which the application
  can write to. While one thread waits for events on an empty ring,
  another one can move the head back so that the ring looks full and
  have a CQE overflow. The waiter can't be stopped any more, not even by
  SIGKILL.

Only the application can make room in the CQ ring. Return to it if the
list could not be flushed.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Reject incomplete...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Reject incomplete event filter expressions

A non-empty expression normally finishes in predicate_parse()'s inner
loop, which resolves the pending logical operators before jumping to
finalization. If the input ends after an operator, possibly followed by
unary '!' tokens, the outer loop instead falls through with unresolved
operator state.

For example, "common_pid == 1 || common_pid == 2 &&" leaves
prog[0].target equal to -1. The second pass then reads prog[-1] before
the forward-jump check can reject it. Depending on adjacent slab
contents, it can also copy an out-of-bounds word into a branch target
that passes the forward-only check. A self-targeted perf tracepoint
counting event can reach this path through PERF_EVENT_IOC_SET_FILTER.

Reject the outer-loop fallthrough when a predicate has already been
parsed. This ensures that non-empty expressions only reach finalization
after the inner loop has resolved their operators. Keep the existing
no-filter error for input that has no predicates. Add a regression test
for trailing logical operators and unary negations.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/damon/core: error...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/damon/core: error damos_commit_quota_goal() for zero target_value

Patch series "mm/damon: move zero damos quota target_value handling to the
core layer".

Having zero DAMOS quota target value can cause division by zero.  DAMON
API callers are checking the target value parameters to avoid that.  It is
easy to make mistakes in some of the multiple API callers.  Move that to
the core layer.

Patch 1 adds the corner case handling into the core layer DAMON parameters
validation logic.  Patches 2 and 3 remove no more needed DAMON API callers
side handling of the corner case in DAMON_LRU_SORT and DMON_SAMPLIE_MTIER,
respectively.


This patch (of 3):

If a DAMOS scheme has a damos_quota_goal of zero target_value,
damos_quota_goal() could trigger division-by-zero error.  Hence each DAMON
API callers should do the zero target_value validation.  It is easy to
make mistakes.  Actually such bugs in DAMON_LRU_SORT and
DAMON_SAMPLE_MTIER were found and fixed [1].

It is better to handle the corner case only once in the core layer,
instead of multiple places in all DAMON API callers.  One straightforward
option is using an alternative denominator for the corner case in the
damos_quota_goal().  However, the zero target_value is meaningless.  In
this case, the quota goal is always evaluated as achieved or
over-achieved.  The quota will only keep being reduced.

Simply avoid using zero target_value by adding a check in the core layer
DAMOS quota goal parameters validation/commit path,
damos_commit_quota_goal().  Update it to return an error in the case. 
Also update its caller to propagate the error.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: don't lose...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: don't lose the signal that ends work

When a thread exits, only its tracked requests are cancelled. Then its
io-wq is torn down. io_wq_exit_workers() signals every worker, to get it
out of an interruptible sleep, and waits for all of them to exit. Before
they do, they go through the work that is left. Unbounded work is
cancelled. Bounded work is run, as it is expected to end by itself.

Not all of it does. An open has no file yet, so it counts as bounded, and
the open of a FIFO waits for the other end. That is what the signal is for.
But the workers are signalled once, and a worker that hasn't started the
work by then loses the signal:

  io_wq_exit_workers()               io_worker_handle_work()
    io_wq_worker_wake()
      set TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL
                                       io_assign_current_work()
                                         io_run_task_work()
                                           clear TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL
                                       io_wq_submit_work()
                                         fifo_open()
                                           wait_for_partner()
    wait_for_completion_timeout()

The thread never gets out of do_exit():

  IORING_OP_OPENAT of a FIFO without a writer, IOSQE_ASYNC
  exit of the thread that has submitted it

hangs in more than 9 of 10 attempts (4 CPUs, KVM), until the process is
killed.

Set TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL for bounded work that is started with IO_WQ_BIT_EXIT
set. The bit is set before the workers are signalled, and it is tested
after the flag has been cleared, with clear_notify_signal() providing the
barrier. So either the flag stays, or the bit is seen.

Work that is started while the io-wq exits is treated like work that is
being run at that time: it isn't interrupted unless it waits
interruptibly.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

keys: Avoid the owner...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

keys: Avoid the owner account dereference in named keyring lookup

Named keyring lookup must keep the storage containing the owner UID
alive through the namespace mapping check.  find_keyring_by_name()
reads keyring->user->uid under keyring_name_lock, but that lock protects
the keyring's name entry and allocation, not its separate key_user.

A named session-keyring join can overlap a privileged KEYCTL_CHOWN on
another CPU.  If the keyring holds the last reference to its old dynamic
key_user and the ownership transfer succeeds, the following ordering is
possible:

    Named join                         Chown
    find_keyring_by_name()              keyctl_chown_key()
      read_lock(keyring_name_lock)       down_write(key->sem)
      load old keyring->user
                                         replace key->user and key->uid
                                         up_write(key->sem)
                                         key_put(key)
                                         key_user_put(old user): free
      read old user->uid
      read_unlock(keyring_name_lock)

Chown neither takes keyring_name_lock nor key_session_mutex, so it can
free the old account between the pointer load and the UID read.  The
lookup then reads freed memory even though the keyring itself is alive.

Use keyring->uid for the mapping check.  key_alloc() initializes this
inline owner UID and keyctl_chown_key() updates it on chown.
The existing name lock keeps its containing keyring allocated throughout
the check, so lookup no longer depends on the account's lifetime.  This
also matches the owner UID used by the permission check.

KASAN report as below:

    BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in find_keyring_by_name+0x577/0x5d0
    Read of size 4 at addr ffff8881128ae2ec by task keycase/500

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/cmd: don't leave...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/cmd: don't leave list poison in ->hash_node

io_uring_cmd_del_cancelable() uses hlist_del() to take a command off
->cancelable_uring_cmd, which leaves LIST_POISON1/2 behind in
->hash_node. Requests are recycled through the request cache without
being reinitialised, and not every user of ->hash_node sets it up before
it is used:

If a vectored futex wait is woken while futex_wait_multiple_setup() is
still queueing the futexes, io_futexv_wait() doesn't add the request to
->futex_list, and leaves the completion to the task_work queued by the
wake up. io_futexv_complete() ends in __io_futex_complete(), whose
hlist_del_init() is fine for a request that is unhashed, which is how all
other users of the node leave it. If the request was a cancelable
uring_cmd in its previous life, e.g. a ublk FETCH_REQ, it writes through
LIST_POISON2:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access in range [0xdead000000000120-...]
  RIP: 0010:io_futexv_complete+0x219/0x420
  Call Trace:
   tctx_task_work_run+0x804/0x950
   tctx_task_work+0x71/0xa0
   task_work_run+0x118/0x200

Leave the node unhashed.

advisories.description: A flaw was found in the DPDK GSO library. When software GSO copies packet headers into a new mbuf, it does not check that the header fits in the source first segment or in the destination buffer, and a header longer than the configured GSO segment size can underflow the payload-size calculation. A remote or guest-supplied packet processed with software GSO can trigger an out-of-bounds read or write.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in the DPDK vhost library. When handling a virtio indirect descriptor table, the...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in the DPDK vhost library. When handling a virtio indirect descriptor table, the host reads the table length more than once from guest memory and can allocate a host copy before validating that length. A guest that changes the length between those reads, or that supplies an out-of-range next index on a small host copy in the vDPA relay path, can cause the host vhost process to walk past the validated mapping or heap copy. That can crash or disrupt the vhost process. Out-of-bounds bytes are consumed as descriptor fields for GPA translation and are not returned to the guest as payload. This is a residual issue in the non-contiguous indirect descriptor copy path introduced as part of the CVE-2018-1059 fix.

advisories.description: TinyUSB through 0.21.0, fixed in commit e85c2b8, contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the MTP device class helper mtp_container_get_string() in src/class/mtp/mtp.h that allows a malicious USB host to corrupt adjacent memory by supplying a crafted MTP string with an unbounded character count. Attackers can exploit the unchecked memcpy operation copying up to 510 bytes into a fixed-size destination buffer to achieve code execution or cause a denial of service on the TinyUSB MTP device.

advisories.summary: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity (CWE-1333) in generate_regex() (whatstk/whatsapp/parser...
advisories.description: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity (CWE-1333) in generate_regex() (whatstk/whatsapp/parser.py) in whatstk from 0.2.0 before 0.9.0 allows a party that supplies a chat export to consume the CPU of the process that parses it for an unbounded time, because the function builds the header regular expression by replacing each %x code with its named capture group and leaves every other character of the header format in the pattern unescaped. A header whose date separator is a regular expression metacharacter therefore alters the pattern instead of matching itself: a separator of + quantifies the preceding capture group, giving (?P<day>\d{1,2})+(?P<month>\d{1,2})+(?P<year>\d{2,4}), and a run of digits that cannot complete the header then makes the engine try every way of partitioning that run. Header auto detection is enabled by default and derives the format from the text of the file, so the separator is taken from the export itself and no header format has to be passed by the caller. Separators of (, ) and \ instead raise re.PatternError, separators of *, | and ? raise TypeError, and separators of ^ and $ raise KeyError, none of which the library catches. This results in the parse of a file of a few hundred bytes consuming CPU without completing, or in an uncaught exception in the calling program.

Successful

is presented to a target user as a legitimate Tapo event, retrieve internal
service information through crafted proxy requests, or abuse Tapo Cloud
outbound request capability in activity that could affect service
availability.
